newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen futures end sharply higher on tankan.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen futures end sharply higher on tankan.

text.p: Key December three-month euroyen deposit rate futures ended Wednesday's TIFFE day session sharply higher following the release of the Bank of Japan's key "tankan" corporate survey for March.
The December settled at 99.10, after trading between 98.93 and 99.14. Day session turnover was a hefty 124,357.
Euroyen futures received an additional boost in the afternoon from a jump in Japanese government bond (JGB) prices.
"Euroyen futures rose in the morning as the tankan showed a weaker-than-expected business condition in the non-manufacturing sector," said a brokerage house trader.
The March tankan showed an improvement in the closely watched diffusion index (DI) for major manufacturers to plus two, compared with minus three in November.
However, the DI for major non-manufacturers fell to minus six from zero in the previous survey.
JGBs jumped in the afternoon on a local media report that Finance Ministry's (MOF) Trust Fund Bureau will shift its investment focus to holding JGBs for five years and longer.
"Some players, including foreigners, bought euroyen futures following the MOF report to cut losses on short positions," said a trust bank trader.
The December settled off its intraday high as JGB futures pared gains by the close. A rise in Tokyo stocks also capped the key contract's upside, traders said.
"Following the tankan, the December is likely to be solidly supported at around 99.00. It may test 99.15 in the near future," said the brokerage house trader.
The BOJ drained 500 billion yen from the money market on Wednesday morning.
